# pantechdynamics_dns_record (Resource)

A record set in a Pantech DNS zone: every value of one name and type, such as the A records of www. Create and update wait until the change is live on Pantech's name servers (status "active"), usually within a minute. In a zone that is not active yet (awaiting delegation) records stay pending until it is: the wait then ends at once with a warning, and the record is kept. Names and values are compared the way the DNS server compares them, so "Mail.Example.com" and "mail.example.com." are the same value and do not show a change. The apex SOA and NS records are managed by Pantech DNS and cannot be managed here. At most 10,000 record sets per zone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pantechdynamics_dns_zone" "example" {
  name = "example.com"
}

# Two A records for www. Values are a set: their order does not matter.
resource "pantechdynamics_dns_record" "www" {
  zone_id = pantechdynamics_dns_zone.example.id
  name    = "www"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 300
  values  = ["203.0.113.10", "203.0.113.11"]
}

# Mail for the zone apex ("@"). Host names may be written with or without the
# trailing dot; the plan does not show a change either way.
resource "pantechdynamics_dns_record" "mx" {
  zone_id = pantechdynamics_dns_zone.example.id
  name    = "@"
  type    = "MX"
  values  = ["10 mail.example.com", "20 backup-mail.example.com"]
}

# A long TXT value is split into 255-byte strings for you.
resource "pantechdynamics_dns_record" "spf" {
  zone_id = pantechdynamics_dns_zone.example.id
  name    = "@"
  type    = "TXT"
  values  = ["v=spf1 include:_spf.example.com -all"]
  comment = "Mail senders"
}

# A private address needs allow_private, for a name only VPC hosts resolve.
resource "pantechdynamics_dns_record" "db" {
  zone_id       = pantechdynamics_dns_zone.example.id
  name          = "db.internal"
  type          = "A"
  values        = ["10.0.1.20"]
  allow_private = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name relative to the zone: "@" for the zone apex, "www", "*.dev" for a wildcard, "_dmarc". A fully-qualified name ending in the zone and a dot ("www.example.com.") is accepted too. Changing it replaces the record set.
- `type` (String) Record type: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, CAA, NS, PTR. NS is for delegating a subdomain only. Changing it replaces the record set.
- `values` (Set of String) The answers, 1 to 100. Formats: A "203.0.113.10"; AAAA "2001:db8::1"; CNAME, NS and PTR a host name; MX "10 mail.example.com"; SRV "10 5 5060 sip.example.com"; CAA `0 issue "ca.example.net"`; TXT any printable text up to 4000 bytes (long text is split into 255-byte strings for you). A CNAME has exactly one value and cannot be at the apex. Private and carrier-grade NAT addresses need allow_private.
- `zone_id` (String) Id of the zone (dnsz_...). Changing it replaces the record set.

### Optional

- `allow_private` (Boolean) Allow private and carrier-grade NAT addresses in A and AAAA values, for names that resolve to VPC addresses. Defaults to false.
- `comment` (String) A note for yourself, at most 255 characters. It is not published in DNS. Defaults to "".
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `ttl` (Number) How long resolvers may cache the answer, in seconds, 60 to 86400. Defaults to 300.

### Read-Only

- `fqdn` (String) The fully-qualified name, without a trailing dot, such as "www.example.com".
- `id` (String) Identifier of the record set, starting with dnsr_.
- `status` (String) State of the record set: "pending" while a change is applied, "active", "deleting" or "failed".
- `version` (Number) Version of the record set. Every update is sent with it as If-Match, so a change made elsewhere since the last refresh is refused instead of overwritten.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A record set is imported as "<zone_id>/<record_id>", or by name and type as
# "<zone_id>/<name>/<type>" ("@" is the zone apex).
terraform import pantechdynamics_dns_record.www dnsz_06ggf2abcdefghjkmnpqrstvw/dnsr_06ggf3abcdefghjkmnpqrstvw
terraform import pantechdynamics_dns_record.mx dnsz_06ggf2abcdefghjkmnpqrstvw/@/MX
```
